lemma_past_closedness.statement: Let q be a point of the conformal completion and let gamma: [0,T) -> M be a future-directed causal curve. If some tail gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q) intersect M for some t0 in [0,T), then the whole curve gamma([0,T)) is contained in J^-(q) intersect M.
hypotheses: the causal relation used to define J^-(q) is the standard future-directed causal-precedence relation of the conformal completion (Mtilde, gtilde)
causal precedence is transitive (concatenation of future-directed causal curves is a future-directed causal curve)
gamma is future-directed causal, so for t < t0 the segment gamma|[t,t0] is a future-directed causal curve from gamma(t) to gamma(t0)
lemma_past_closedness.proof: Fix t in [0,t0). By hypothesis gamma(t0) is in J^-(q), so gamma(t0) precedes q. The segment gamma|[t,t0] is a future-directed causal curve from gamma(t) to gamma(t0). By transitivity gamma(t) precedes q, hence gamma(t) is in J^-(q). Points with t >= t0 are in J^-(q) by hypothesis. Therefore gamma([0,T)) is a subset of J^-(q). The converse is immediate with t0 = 0.
lemma_past_closedness.corollary: For every future-inextendible causal geodesic gamma of finite affine length: [exists q in I+ with gamma subset J^-(q) intersect M] if and only if [exists q in I+ and t0 in [0,T) with the tail gamma([t0,T)) subset J^-(q) intersect M]. Negating both sides: the whole-curve clause 'not exists q in I+ with gamma subset J^-(q) intersect M' in quantifiers.formal is logically equivalent to the tail clause 'for every q in I+ and every t0 in [0,T), the tail is not contained in J^-(q) intersect M' in visibility.negation_conclusion.
lemma_past_closedness.consequence: quantifiers.formal and quantifiers.negation ARE exact negations of each other on the pinned bytes. The phrase 'strictly weaker' in the ADJ-1 allegation is false as a statement about the class extension; the class extension is unchanged whether visibility is written with the whole-curve or the tail clause.
lemma_past_closedness.counterexample_search_note: The only way to break the lemma is to deny past-closedness/transitivity of J^-(q) for the schema's declared causal structure, or to use a non-causal curve; neither is admitted by D4 (future-directed causal geodesics) or by the standard definition of J^- used in visibility.definition.

adjudication.source: reviews/F1-review-19.json hard_failures[0] (worker deepseek-flash-19), alleged critical: quantifiers.formal is strictly weaker than the canonical tail predicate; formal and negation are not exact negations

measured.formal_text: not exists q in I+ with gamma subset J^-(q) intersect M
measured.D5_text: points q of I+ such that gamma([0,T)) is contained in the causal past J^-(q) intersected with M
measured.visibility_text: exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that the TAIL gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q) intersect M

adjudication.rationale: The pinned text does use whole-curve containment where visibility.definition uses the tail, so the wording difference is real. However LEMMA-W026-1 proves the two containment clauses are equivalent for exactly the geodesics D4 admits, because J^-(q) is past-closed and the causal relation is transitive. Therefore the class extension is unchanged and the formal clause is the exact negation of the tail predicate. The reviewer's inference from wording difference to a different class extension rests on the false premise that a curved causal geodesic can have a tail inside J^-(q) without the whole curve being inside J^-(q).
adjudication.surviving_part: documentation precision (N): (a) visibility.definition's sentence 'requiring the whole geodesic to lie in J^-(q) would misclassify a geodesic that starts in the exterior and ends inside the black-hole region' does not discriminate the two formulations: for that example both readings classify the geodesic as not visible, so the stated justification is a non-sequitur; (b) quantifiers.formal/D5 do not state the equivalence lemma, and the omission demonstrably misled a competent reviewer (worker-019) - and reader-disagreement is one of the schema's own declared falsifiers (falsifier.schema_falsifiers[0]).
adjudication.recommended_minimal_fix: Add one line to quantifiers (and/or visibility.definition): 'the whole-curve and tail clauses are equivalent because J^-(q) is past-closed and gamma is causal (LEMMA-W026-1)'; replace the misclassification sentence with that equivalence statement. No change to the class extension, quantifier order, or conclusion type is required.

adjudication.recommended_minimal_fix: Either expand the two shorthands inline in statement_formal or add a notation table mapping AF_{I+}(M_D) -> i_plus.definition and complete(I+_D) -> i_plus.completeness_definition.

adjudication.source: reviews/F1-review-094.json hard_failures[0] HF-094-2 (worker-094), alleged major: duplicate YAML mapping keys and future-dated timestamps
